open_task_policy: Accept every correct proof under the actual hypotheses, including short proofs using applicable background theorems. Author proof order, counterexamples, vocabulary and length are not mandatory. Explicitly conditional contributions are distinct from completing the original task; honest incompleteness is distinct from invalid proof.
required_evidence: Construct the actual inverse-limit ring and show that its augmentation is independent of the chosen nonempty directed index.
Prove that every finite complete orthogonal idempotent family of S has exactly one such family in L, while respecting stagewise nil kernels and the arbitrary directed index.
Construct the requested canonical product-of-quotients ring isomorphism from the lifted family.
Construct the induced map of inverse limits for a compatible system morphism and prove naturality of the finite-family bijections.
critical_errors: Infer that the kernel of the limit augmentation consists of nilpotent elements from the stagewise nil hypotheses; the truncated-polynomial tower disproves this.
Infer that the limit augmentation or transition maps are surjective merely from the stage augmentations being surjective.
Choose unrelated lifts at each level and assert compatibility before using idempotency and unique lifting.
Replace element-dependent nilpotence by one exponent annihilating the entire kernel, one exponent uniform in i, finite generation, or a Noetherian assumption.
Use division by 2 or an invertibility assumption not justified in arbitrary characteristic.
Lift each idempotent but fail to establish mutual orthogonality or that the sum of the lifts equals 1.
Assert a ring direct-sum splitting or canonical lifts for all elements of S from the much narrower idempotent classification.
Require nonzero idempotents or nonempty J, or assume the base map of a system morphism is injective/surjective.
completion_policy: The finite-family classification, quotient-factor isomorphism and naturality are all main obligations. A short correct rigidity-based proof is sufficient. The three author-side counterexamples are not candidate obligations; no formal power-series identification or nilpotence of the limit kernel is requested.
